title: About
text:
I grew up in Bangladesh and studied economics at Noakhali Science & Technology University, where I finished both my bachelor’s and master’s degrees before teaching for two years at National Model College.
I then spent three years at Bangladesh Honda Private Limited in corporate affairs and safety, first as an Executive and later as a Senior Executive. That period taught me a great deal about how firms actually make decisions under regulatory and operational constraints — something I still think about when I read finance papers.
In 2023 I moved to Texas for an M.S. in Economics at the University of North Texas, concentrating in econometrics and quantitative methods, and I am now in the finance PhD program at Old Dominion University in Norfolk, Virginia.

title: Ahsan Habib
text:
I am a doctoral student in Business Administration with a concentration in Finance at the Strome College of Business, Old Dominion University.
My research sits at the intersection of asset pricing, financial economics, corporate finance and geopolitical risk . I am currently working on how the defense sector prices different components of geopolitical risk, and on the economic consequences of climate change for the Chesapeake Bay fishery.
Before starting the PhD I completed an M.S. in Economics (Econometrics and Quantitative Economics) at the University of North Texas, and worked senior executive in corporate affairs at Bangladesh Honda Private Limited.
Research interests

Asset pricing and the cross-section of returns
Geopolitical and climate risk in financial markets

title: Research
text: My work asks how investors price risks that sit outside the standard factor models — geopolitical conflict, climate exposure, and structural shifts in resource economies.

title: Research
text:
Working Papers
What type of geopolitical risk do defense stocks hedge? A sub-index decomposition of the defense premium
Ahsan Habib
Prepared for the CRT Young Researcher Hunt 2026.

Defense equities are widely treated as a single hedge against “geopolitical risk,” but the risk index itself is a composite. This paper decomposes the index into its sub-components to ask which specific categories of risk the defense premium actually compensates for.


Climate change and the Chesapeake Bay fishery industry: An integrated ecological and economic impact assessment
Ahsan Habib and Wai Yan Siu
Manuscript in preparation. Funded by the ODU Graduate Summer Award Program (GSAP) 2026.

An integrated assessment linking ecological projections for the Chesapeake Bay to the economic outcomes of the commercial fishery that depends on it.
